annotations.title: Prepare the statements of a tenant estoppel certificate

description: Prepare the standard statements of a tenant estoppel certificate from verified lease facts, for a lender or buyer who wants the tenant to confirm the lease. Give the lease's facts (doc_abstract_lease or doc_verify_facts, each with its quote and page and passing fact_validate: parties, commencement and expiration, rentable area, base rent schedule, security deposit, free rent, TI allowance, renewal, expansion, termination and purchase options and their notice deadlines), the lease and amendment documents, the premises and as_of, and optionally what the landlord's own records say (rent paid through, deposit held). Returns numbered statements: the lease and amendment list with document fingerprints, commencement, expiration, premises, current base rent and the next step (annual and monthly, worked and shown), security deposit, free rent, TI allowance, each option, each carrying the source quote and page, with a superseded sentence shown as superseded when an amendment changed it; and statements only the tenant can know (no other agreements, deposit paid, rent paid through, no rent paid more than one month ahead, landlord obligations outstanding, no other options, no landlord default, no tenant default, no assignment or sublease), marked tenant to confirm with no lease source. Flags every gap (a term the facts do not supply) and every conflict between the lease and an amendment, and withholds that statement rather than guess. Also returns key figures, totals, package_facts and package_items ready for fact_package_send kind estoppel. Deterministic and no model: same facts, same statements; as_of is an input. These are facts and arithmetic, not legal advice, and the tenant's signature, not FactLot, is what makes a certificate an estoppel. Each statement carries its quote, for a person to review before anything is sent. On the hosted API the whole answer also carries attestation, the service's signature over the items, grades and figures that fact_package_send carries, so the FactLot record can show them as computed by FactLot and unchanged since; a service without a signing key returns none and says so. On the hosted API, callers without a Pro or Team key get the summary only (counts, statement titles and status, gaps and conflicts) and the answer says what is withheld. Each free, email-verified account (an fl_free_ key) gets one whole document in total across audit_expense_statement, estoppel_prepare and rent_roll_certify: that answer says so, and the report built from the same arguments is included for 24 hours; Pro and Team include every document with the monthly allowance.

as_of.description: The date of the certificate, YYYY-MM-DD. The tool reads no clock: the current rent step and the next one are found from this date.

documents.description: Optional: which cited document is the lease and which are amendments. Without it, a document whose facts carry valid_from is an amendment and the one remaining is the lease; anything unclear is flagged, never guessed.

document_id.description: The document's FactLot ID, as the facts cite it.

effective_date.description: For an amendment, the date it takes effect.

landlord_records.description: Optional figures from the landlord's own records. They have no lease source and are marked as the landlord's.

rent_paid_through.description: The date through which the landlord's own ledger shows rent paid. It is not a lease term: it is shown to the tenant as the landlord's figure to confirm.

security_deposit_held.description: The deposit the landlord's ledger shows held, USD. Compared with the lease's figure; a difference is flagged. Must be greater than 0.

lease_facts.description: The lease's verified facts, for the lease and every amendment (doc_abstract_lease's facts, or doc_verify_facts' verified[].fact), each with its quote and page and passing fact_validate. Read by predicate: lease.landlord, lease.tenant, lease.commencement_date, lease.expiration_date, lease.rentable_area_sf, lease.base_rent_schedule (dated steps {from, to, annual_rent_psf}), lease.security_deposit (USD), lease.free_rent {months, applies_to}, lease.ti_allowance (USD, or {amount, per_sf?}), lease.renewal_option {count, term_months, notice_months, rent}, lease.renewal_notice_deadline, lease.termination_option {effective_date, notice_months, fee}, lease.termination_notice_deadline, lease.expansion_option (text or {description}), lease.expansion_option_deadline, lease.rofr and lease.rofo {applies_to: space|purchase, description, response_days}, lease.purchase_option (text or {description, price?}). A fact another fact supersedes (supersedes) is history; a fact valid_from after as_of is pending and not used. A term no fact supplies is listed under gaps; nothing is guessed.

landlord.description: The landlord the certificate is given about.

organisation.description: The organisation's name as the lease or the certificate uses it.

requested_by.description: The lender or buyer the certificate is for, if known. The tenant's answers are for it to rely on; it is not the sender.

organisation.description: The organisation's name as the lease or the certificate uses it.

tenant.description: The tenant that will sign the certificate.

organisation.description: The organisation's name as the lease or the certificate uses it.

label.description: The premises in words: address and suite.
